pericopes.text: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta. The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold. But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand. When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said one to another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.” However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed. But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

echoes.text: You will tread on the lion and cobra. You will trample the young lion and the serpent underfoot.
echoes.note: Paul gathers sticks, a viper fastens on his hand, yet he shakes it off unharmed. The promise that the righteous one 'will tread on the adder' and trample serpent and viper without harm (LXX Ps 90:13) is the closest scriptural template for the scene: deadly snake, divine protection, no injury. The vocabulary of viper/serpent and the motif of the protected servant give strong thematic coherence at the book's climax.

echoes.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
echoes.note: The protoevangelium's enmity between humanity and the serpent — the serpent striking at the heel/hand while the human ultimately prevails — resonates with Paul's hand bitten yet the creature destroyed in the fire. Reversal of the primal serpent-bite is figurally apt for the apostle's vindication.

echoes.text: Yahweh sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people. Many people of Israel died. The people came to Moses, and said, “We have sinned, because we have spoken against Yahweh, and against you. Pray to Yahweh, that he take away the serpents from us.” Moses prayed for the people. Yahweh said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent, and set it on a pole. It shall happen, that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.” Moses made a serpent of […]
echoes.note: The fiery serpents that bit Israel in the wilderness and the bronze serpent of deliverance supply a background motif of snakebite and divinely-granted survival; verbal overlap is slight, link is thematic.

echoes.text: who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, with fiery serpents and scorpions, and thirsty ground where there was no water; who poured water for you out of the rock of flint;
echoes.note: The wilderness journey 'with its fiery serpents' from which God preserved Israel parallels the survivor of shipwreck preserved from the venomous bite; a faint provision-and-protection echo.

echoes.text: For even when terrible raging of wild beasts came upon your people, And they were perishing by the bites of crooked serpents, Your wrath continued not to the uttermost; But for admonition were they troubled for a short space, Having a token of salvation, To put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law: For he that turned toward it was not saved because of that which was seen, But because of you, the Saviour of all. Yes, and in this did you […]
echoes.note: Deuterocanonical reflection on Numbers 21: God's people bitten by serpents are healed not by what they saw but by God the Savior, while their bites were not fatal because of divine mercy. The pattern of harmless venom for the righteous coheres with Paul shaking off the viper unharmed.

pericopes.text: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days. The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him. Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured. They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

echoes.text: When Elisha had come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and laid on his bed. He went in therefore, and shut the door on them both, and prayed to Yahweh. He went up, and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretched himself on him; and the flesh of the child grew warm. Then he returned, and walked in the house once back and forth; and went up, and stretched himself on him. Then […]
echoes.note: Paul enters in to the sick father of Publius, prays, lays hands on him and heals him; the Elisha pattern of a prophet entering the sickroom and praying for restoration supplies a background healing-narrative template, with the further healings of all the island's sick recalling the prophet's wider miracles.

echoes.text: Then you shall see and be radiant, and your heart shall thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be turned to you, the wealth of the nations shall come to you. The multitude of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come; they shall bring gold and frankincense, and shall proclaim the praises of Yahweh. All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together to you, the rams of Nebaioth shall […]
echoes.note: The islanders 'honored us with many honors' and stocked the ship with provisions; the prophetic vision of the isles/coastlands bringing their wealth and gifts to God's servants offers a faint figural resonance with Gentiles honoring the apostolic party.

pericopes.text: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was “The Twin Brothers.” Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days. From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli, where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome. From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage. When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

echoes.text: “Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.
echoes.note: When the Roman brothers come to meet him 'Paul thanked God and took courage'; the recurrent OT exhortation to 'be strong and take courage' before entering the appointed place colors his renewed resolve on arrival at Rome, though the verbal link is general.

pericopes.text: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans, who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me. But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation. For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.” They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you. But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

echoes.text: You hope of Israel, its Savior in the time of trouble, why should you be as a foreigner in the land, and as a wayfaring man who turns aside to stay for a night?
echoes.note: Paul declares he is bound 'because of the hope of Israel.' The phrase 'hope of Israel' is a direct Jeremianic title for the LORD ('O hope of Israel, its savior in time of trouble'), giving real verbal coherence to Paul's self-defense.

echoes.text: Yahweh, the hope of Israel, all who forsake you shall be disappointed. Those who depart from me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken Yahweh, the spring of living waters.
echoes.note: A second Jeremianic occurrence — 'O LORD, the hope of Israel' — reinforces the title behind Paul's claim; recurrence of the phrase across Jeremiah strengthens the allusion.

pericopes.text: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about the Kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening. Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved. When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word, “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers, saying, ‘Go to this people, and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive. For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, and I would heal them.’ “Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the nations. They will also listen.”

echoes.text: He said, “Go, and tell this people, ‘You hear indeed, but don’t understand; and you see indeed, but don’t perceive.’ Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”
echoes.note: The climactic citation that seals the book: 'Go to this people and say, In hearing you will hear but not understand... lest they turn and I would heal them.' Acts 28:26-27 reproduces LXX Isaiah 6:9-10 almost verbatim, explicitly attributed ('the Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet'). Maximal volume and an introductory formula — the keystone quotation.

echoes.text: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
echoes.note: 'The salvation of God is sent to the nations' echoes the Servant commission to be 'a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth' — a programmatic Isaianic text Luke uses elsewhere; here it interprets the turn to the Gentiles immediately after the Isaiah 6 hardening oracle.

echoes.text: That your way may be known on earth, and your salvation among all nations,
echoes.note: 'That your way may be known on earth, your saving power among all nations' (LXX Ps 66:3) supplies the universal-salvation idiom behind 'the salvation of God is sent to the nations... they will also listen.'

echoes.text: Yahweh has made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
echoes.note: 'All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God' reinforces the Gentile-salvation declaration; the phrase 'salvation of God' coheres closely with Paul's closing words.

echoes.text: Yahweh has made known his salvation. He has openly shown his righteousness in the sight of the nations. He has remembered his loving kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has made known his salvation... all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God' is another psalmic source for the 'salvation of God' to the nations motif behind v.28.

pericopes.text: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves. Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who were coming to him, preaching the Kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

echoes.text: It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of Yahweh’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it. Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
echoes.note: Paul's unhindered preaching of the Kingdom of God in the imperial capital, with all who come received, gives a faint figural fulfillment of the nations streaming to learn God's ways; the link is thematic, not verbal.
